title: Bread, wheat or cracked wheat, homemade or bakery purchase

content.title: About
content.content: Bread made from wheat or cracked wheat is a baked product prepared from whole grain wheat, whole‑grain flour or coarsely ground wheat. It can be homemade or bought from a bakery. The loaf features a distinctive aroma, a dense crumb and a lightly crisp crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for more than 10,000 years.
Cracked wheat retains most of the bran and germ, boosting the nutritional value of the bread.
Homemade bread often undergoes a longer fermentation, enhancing flavor and aroma.
Traditional bakeries frequently use sourdough starter instead of commercial yeast for better taste and digestibility.
Whole‑wheat bread contains more fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals than white bread.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting gut health and promoting satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat delivers slow‑releasing glucose, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and folate in whole‑grain bread aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc contribute to muscle function, blood formation and immune health.

items.title: Probiotic effect of sourdough
items.content: Sourdough bread contains lactic‑acid bacteria that may improve intestinal microbiota.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions or gluten sensitivity, leading to digestive discomfort.

items.title: High glycemic index of white bread
items.content: Bread made from refined flour can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, which is undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain breads contain significant amounts of salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Mold and mycotoxins
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth, producing toxins harmful to health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be eaten plain, used for sandwiches, served with soups, made into toast, croutons or breadcrumbs. For extra flavor, toast slices and add olive oil, avocado or a spread of your choice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag and thaw in a toaster or oven. Avoid moisture to prevent mold growth.
